answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Memory_31 and memory_86 both show that simplifying and shortening onboarding drives measurable improvements in activation and completion rates. These are the most directly relevant to our current metrics decline. We should verify these two records to confirm the magnitude and durability of their effects before running a new experiment. Simplify_onboarding is lower-risk than promotional_pricing (which could harm margins and doesn't address the core activation problem) and is more immediately actionable than enterprise_sales_assist (which targets a different segment). The referral_incentive worked well for established customers (memory_57) but won't help recover lost new-account activation. Activation_messaging (memory_91) showed promise but onboarding friction appears to be a root cause we can address structurally. A standard_experiment scale allows us to test the effect on both SMB accounts and measure whether simplified onboarding can recover the 4-6% lift we've lost, while preserving the option to iterate or pivot based on results.
